pick.name: AWS BAA via AWS Artifact + Amazon Bedrock (Claude) for PHI
pick.what: Accept the AWS BAA yourself in AWS Artifact; keep PHI only in HIPAA-eligible services
pick.why: Self-serve BAA with no plan minimum (Google Cloud's is also self-accept), and Claude runs on HIPAA-eligible Bedrock; no sales call needed
pick.free_limits: BAA acceptance itself appears free; pay-as-you-go service costs

decision: Most free-tier picks in the default stack (Cloudflare Workers/R2, Neon Free, Resend, PostHog Free, Sentry Developer) are not BAA-covered, so PHI must never touch them. For a healthcare client, run a separate PHI stack on AWS under the self-accepted BAA (Bedrock for Claude, RDS/S3/SES/Lambda) and sign Common Paper's BAA downstream. Paid BAA paths if you'd rather stay on the
details: A BAA does not make you compliant; you still need risk analysis, access controls, audit logs and policies. Verify with a lawyer.

verify.note: Correct: BAA accepted in AWS Artifact, no plan stated, and Bedrock (plus AgentCore), RDS, S3, Lambda, SES and CloudFront are on the HIPAA-eligible list. Wrong: 'only self-serve BAA among the big clouds'. Google Cloud's BAA is also self-accepted in the console (IAM & Admin > Privacy > Review and Accept). The AWS pick still stands because Claude is on Bedrock. Sentry is also missing from the not-covered list: its Developer/Team plans have no BAA, only Business+.
